frontMatter.value: Give sparse, evidence-based progress updates during long-running work: observable milestones weighted by work and risk, an update only when something material changed, one rounded-down bar. Use while long work with several milestones runs between replies, never for a short answer or work with no intermediate state; and the moment the owner asks to change how or how often you report progress, whether more updates, total silence or an estimated clock, BEFORE any such preference is saved anywhere.

passages.text:
progress-check is the habit for the moment long work runs between replies: a
change with several milestones, a build of many slices, delegated agents
running one after another. It never fires on a short answer or on work whose
only honest states are started and finished, and its cadence is judgment,
never spam. It also fires the moment the owner asks to change how or how often
you report, whether more updates, silence or an estimated clock: follow the
preference within the current task, keep reporting actionable blockers, and
save nothing anywhere unless the owner asks for a lasting rule (Persist a
preference, below). It writes no record of its own: progress stays in the
conversation, the evidence behind it belongs to the change record's sections
and the checks the change recorded, and an estimated clock is an
unmeasured claim this habit never makes.
passages.reason: The opening paragraph in the habit's own voice: the situations its block rows key it by, long work running between replies (a change with several milestones, a build of many slices, delegated agents one after another) and the owner asking to change how or how often progress is reported; never a short answer or two-state work, on a cadence that is judgment; that it writes no record of its own, the evidence being the change record's and its checks'; and that an estimated clock is never claimed. Re-cut at S18b onto the change record, in place of a ticket held at implementing and its execution account. Since J-93 S2 the front names greenline's homes and commands by their nouns, their paths and commands on the skill's references page.
passages.gist: Opens the habit: long work between replies, never a short answer

passages.text:
3. Send a routine update only when turns of work have passed since the previous
   routine update or a step of the change has ended, **and** one of these is
   true: a milestone completed, verified progress rose by at least 10 percentage
   points, or the next action materially changed. Never estimate elapsed time to
   open the gate; an estimated clock is an unmeasured claim.

Re-cut at S18b: the end of a step replaces a ticket's status transition.
passages.gist: Routine updates follow turns of work or a step's end, not minutes

drops.reason: The agent has no wall clock and its unit of reply is the turn, so the 30-minute half of the routine-update gate is re-anchored in SKILL.md step 3 and METHODOLOGY.md section 3 to turns of work since the previous routine update or the end of a step of the change, the change half (a milestone, ten verified points, a different next action) unchanged and an estimated elapsed time never used to open the gate; section 8's open gap names the turn-and-step cadence in place of the 30-minute default and drops the global-install gap that went with the removed mode.
drops.gist: Re-anchors the update gate from thirty minutes to turns of work
